# Phase 02.1: Tighten Visual Density to Design-Reference Fidelity - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-05-07
**Status:** Ready for planning
**Source:** Auto-generated post-Phase-2 follow-up. Triggered by founder review of the as-shipped state vs `design-reference.png`: the long-scroll SPA structure (~12 000 px tall) is significantly different from the reference's compressed single-screen layout (~1 280 px tall, 605 px wide). Phase 2's pixel test passes at 19.57% only because both images are mostly dark; the pages are structurally not the same shape.

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Phase 02.1 is a **vertical-density compression pass** on the existing public landing page. The goal is to bring the SPA's rendered length much closer to `design-reference.png`'s implied density without introducing new sections, new component libraries, new framework adoption, or new locale work.

The reference shows ~10 sections crammed into 1 280 px tall (605 px wide). The current SPA renders the same 10 sections at ~12 000 px tall (1 280 px wide) — every section uses `padding: 140px 0`, the hero is `min-height: 100vh`, and section internals have generous breathing room. Phase 02.1 closes the **structural-density gap** that Phase 2 deliberately did NOT address.

**In phase:**
- Reduce desktop section vertical padding (currently `140px 0`) to a tighter scale; planner picks exact values within the locked spacing system in `src/styles/global.css`
- Reduce hero `min-height: 100vh` to a fixed compact value sized for above-the-fold density (planner picks; suggested ~640–720 px)
- Tighten internal section spacing (heading-to-content gap, between-card gap) where it visibly inflates section height without serving content
- Re-tune the puppeteer + pixelmatch screenshot golden test threshold from `0.22` to a value that reflects the new (much closer) baseline; planner re-runs the empirical tuning protocol from `02-RESEARCH.md` §3 against the post-densification build
- Re-capture and re-document the new diff floor in `02.1-RESEARCH.md`

**Out of phase (handled elsewhere or explicitly excluded):**
- Section consolidation (merging Reviews + Process into one section, dropping FeedStrip, etc.) — explicit anti-feature for v1; Phase 8 polish if needed
- Mobile re-layout (mobile is currently long-scroll by design; Phase 8 mobile audit owns mobile density)
- Copy changes, content edits, real founder photos, real reviews — Phase 8 polish (CONTENT-* requirements)
- Any change to `design-reference.png` itself or to UI-SPEC.md tokens (color, typography roles, weights)
- New component library, shadcn adoption, CSS-in-JS, Tailwind migration, Next.js migration — locked anti-features
- Quiz modal density (already token-aligned in Phase 2 D-03; QuizModal is a transient overlay, not part of the page-density story)
- `CrmProvider` rewrite (Phase 5)

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Density target: pragmatic, not literal

- **D-01:** The target is **"much denser, not literal single-screen."** Aim to compress the SPA's desktop rendered length to **~7 000–8 000 px** (a 33–42% reduction from the ~11 847 px Phase-2 close-out baseline), NOT to the reference's literal ~1 280 px. **Updated 2026-05-07** from initial 5 000–6 000 band after `02.1-RESEARCH.md` empirically demonstrated that the 5 000–6 000 band is unreachable without overriding D-01b (no consolidation) or D-02b (no broad cuts). Rationale: literal single-screen density would force section heights so small that body text becomes unreadable; even pragmatic single-screen-adjacent (5 000–6 000) requires either dropping sections or applying broad within-section cuts beyond the top 3 offenders, which compromises content readability for marginal density gain. ~7 000–8 000 px is the honest pragmatic floor under the locked anti-features.
- **D-01a:** This is Claude's-Discretion bounded by upper and lower bounds. Planner picks the exact target value in the 7 000–8 000 px band based on what the section content actually allows. If the planner's first-pass tuning produces 7 400 px and content still feels cramped, the planner may push to 8 000 px and document the decision in `02.1-RESEARCH.md`. If the planner's first-pass produces 6 800 px without harming readability, that's also acceptable. Anything outside the 6 500–8 500 px band requires a stop-and-confirm with the founder before commit.
- **D-01b:** **Anti-decision (do NOT implement):** literal single-screen compression to ~1 280 px, section consolidation, dropping any of the 10 existing sections, or adding new sections. Those are out of phase.

### Vertical padding scale

- **D-02:** Replace the current `padding: 140px 0` section pattern in `src/styles/global.css` with a tighter scale. The locked spacing system in `global.css` (4-px base, 8/12/16/20/24/32/40/56/72/96 multiples) is the only allowed source. Planner picks the new value (suggested `72px 0` or `80px 0` desktop; `40px 0` or `48px 0` mobile if mobile is touched, which it isn't in this phase per D-04).
- **D-02a:** Hero `min-height: 100vh` becomes a fixed value within the same scale (suggested `640px` or `720px`). The hero is the most aggressive contributor to current page length and the most constrained by the reference's "stats row visible above the fold at 1 280 px tall" demand.
- **D-02b:** Within-section spacing (heading → content gap, card-to-card gap, paragraph spacing) is tightened only where the planner can prove it adds visible empty space without serving comprehension. Each within-section change must be backed by a side-by-side comparison snippet in the plan's `<action>` block. No global "tighten everything by N%" passes.

### Verification gate (re-tuned from Phase 2)

- **D-03:** **Re-run the empirical pixelmatch tuning protocol** from `02-RESEARCH.md` §3 against the post-densification build. Capture the SPA at the same `1280 × 4000 fullPage` viewport, downscale to 605 × 1280 with `sharp.resize({ kernel: 'cubic', fit: 'fill' })`, and `pixelmatch` against `design-reference.png`. The new as-shipped diff floor should be **substantially lower** than 18.74% (Phase 2 floor) — expected band 8–14% based on the reduced page length. Document the empirical floor in `02.1-RESEARCH.md` and tune the new threshold to floor + 3pp safety band.
- **D-03a:** **Update `server/tests/landing-page-golden.test.ts`** in place to use the new `DIFF_THRESHOLD` constant. Do NOT create a parallel test file. The Phase 2 test is the same gate; its threshold value is a tunable.
- **D-03b:** If the post-densification floor is **higher** than 18.74% (regression — densification made things visually worse), STOP and route to a discuss-phase before continuing. This is a falsifiable safety check, not a gate to skip.

### Plan granularity / waves

- **D-04:** **Section-by-section plans where the change is non-trivial; bundled where the change is a single CSS token.** Suggested plan inventory (planner refines):
  - **Wave 0 (foundation):** capture the current density baseline (re-run the empirical tuning protocol against the post-Phase-2 SPA, write `02.1-RESEARCH.md` with the new floor measurement and target threshold). Single deliverable, no source code changes.
  - **Wave 1 (parallelisable):**
    - `global.css` section padding reduction (single utility class change; `.section-padding` or equivalent)
    - Hero `min-height` reduction (`Hero.tsx` inline style or `global.css` rule)
    - Within-section tightening for the visibly-tallest sections (planner identifies via inspection of `bodyHeight` per section)
  - **Wave 2 (gate):** re-tune `DIFF_THRESHOLD` in `landing-page-golden.test.ts`, re-run golden, document final ratio in `02.1-VERIFICATION.md`, close phase.
- **D-04a:** **Mobile is out of scope.** The mobile breakpoint (`@media (max-width: 720px)`) is intentionally NOT touched in this phase. Phase 8 mobile audit owns mobile density. Planner explicitly verifies via grep that no `@media (max-width: 720px)` block was modified.
- **D-04b:** Plans are kept small (single-deliverable, single-section). Each commit must be independently revertable so the founder can roll back any individual change without losing the rest.

### Claude's Discretion

The following are explicitly delegated to the researcher and planner:

- **Exact section padding value** (D-02) — planner picks within the locked spacing system. `72px 0` and `80px 0` are both reasonable; `64px 0` is the lower bound, `96px 0` is the upper bound.
- **Hero min-height value** (D-02a) — `640px` and `720px` are both reasonable.
- **Which sections need within-section tightening** (D-02b) — researcher inspects `getBoundingClientRect()` of each section in puppeteer and reports per-section heights; planner targets the top 3 heaviest if their internal spacing is the cause (vs the section padding alone).
- **New `DIFF_THRESHOLD` value** (D-03) — planner re-runs empirical protocol against post-densification build. Suggested band: 0.10–0.16, but the empirical floor is the only authority.
- **Whether `02-DEFERRED-POLISH.md`'s SuccessStep WhatsApp-brand-vs-success-indicator drift is folded in here or stays in Phase 8** — planner picks based on whether the QuizModal is touched at all. Default: stays in Phase 8 (D-04 keeps quiz scope out).

</decisions>

## Existing Code Insights

### Current density data points (verified 2026-05-07)
- **Total page height at viewport 1280:** ~11 847 px (per `tmp/landing-current-fullpage.png`).
- **Section padding rule:** `padding: 140px 0` on the canonical `.section` utility class in `global.css` (planner verifies exact location and rule name during research).
- **Hero rule:** `min-height: 100vh` (≈ 800–1080 px depending on viewport) — combined with the 140 px section padding on the next section, this puts the hero+gap above 1 000 px on most viewports.
- **Reference target density:** ~10 sections in 1 280 px tall = ~128 px per section average. Pragmatic target (D-01) of ~5 000–6 000 px = ~500–600 px per section average — still 4× denser than current ~1 200 px per section average, still 4× looser than the reference.

### Reusable assets
- **Puppeteer + sharp + pixelmatch + pngjs harness** is already shipped in `server/tests/landing-page-golden.test.ts` (Phase 2 Wave 0). Phase 02.1 re-uses it verbatim — only the `DIFF_THRESHOLD` constant changes.
- **All UI atoms** (`Logo`, `Icon`, `FlagFor`, `Reveal`, `Counter`, `Live`, `Chip`, `CarPlaceholder`, `FounderPortrait`) are stable; do not modify their structure during the density pass.
- **Bespoke CSS token system** in `src/styles/global.css` — all `var(--token)` references already resolve. No new token introduction is required (UI-SPEC §Pre-existing System Note explicitly forbids new font sizes/weights).

### Established patterns
- **Inline styles in TSX + global utility classes** (`.btn`, `.card`, `.h1`, etc.) — extend via additional utility classes, not via CSS-in-JS. Inline for one-off layout. (UI-SPEC §Design System.)
- **Section background alternation between `var(--ink)` and `#0a0a09`** — same color; visual separation comes from `var(--line)` borders, not contrast. Densification must NOT compromise this rhythm — borders stay, alternation stays.
- **House easing `cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)`** — UI-SPEC §Animation. Density pass does not change easing.

### Integration points
- **From this phase to Phase 5:** Same as Phase 2 — `CrmProvider` rewrite must keep `useCrm()` consumer contract from changing. Phase 02.1 does NOT touch `src/crm/`.
- **From this phase to Phase 8:** The deferred-polish list (Phase 2 `02-DEFERRED-POLISH.md`) feeds Phase 8. Phase 02.1 may add 1–2 items to the same file if its 5-min budget rule from Phase 2 D-01a applies.
- **Mobile breakpoint:** `@media (max-width: 720px)` is OFF-LIMITS this phase (D-04a). Phase 8 mobile audit owns it.

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- **The empirical tuning protocol from `02-RESEARCH.md` §3 is reused verbatim.** It worked once; rerun it. The output is a new `DIFF_THRESHOLD` value, nothing else.
- **`design-reference.png` IS still the pixelmatch target.** It does not get replaced or augmented in this phase. The point of the densification is that the SPA, when squashed, is now structurally closer to the reference — so the diff floor drops, and the threshold tightens.
- **Section-level `getBoundingClientRect()` inspection** is the cleanest way to identify which sections are the worst density offenders. Researcher writes a one-off node script (in `tmp/` or as a discardable test fixture) to log per-section heights against the running dev server. This becomes the basis for Wave 1 planning. Output goes into `02.1-RESEARCH.md`, the script is discarded (not committed).
- **The hero is almost certainly the biggest single offender** (`min-height: 100vh`). Reducing it from 100vh to a fixed `640px` or `720px` should drop the page by 200–400 px on a typical 1080p viewport. Quick win.
- **Section padding is the second biggest** (`140px 0` × 10 sections = 2 800 px of padding alone). Reducing to `72px 0` cuts ~1 360 px (10 × 68 px). Largest single change.
- **Within-section tightening** is the third lever. Less impactful, more targeted, riskier (easier to break visual rhythm). Used surgically.
- **The QuizModal is OUT OF PHASE.** If the planner is tempted to fold the deferred SuccessStep gradient drift into a "quick fix" alongside this work, STOP — that's Phase 8.
- **`tmp/landing-current-fullpage.png` and `tmp/landing-current-resized.png`** generated 2026-05-07 are the empirical "before" baseline. They live in `tmp/` (gitignored); the researcher recaptures fresh "after" images at Wave 0.

</specifics>

- **Self-hosting Gilroy fonts** — Phase 8 polish (G-08 deferred from Phase 2).
